about:
Apparel Forge operates a manufacturing facility in Sarasota, Florida, where it maintains complete control over the production process from start to finish. The company produces custom-made apparel and sportswear entirely in-house, emphasizing domestic production.

Its core capabilities include direct-to-film printing and fully custom sublimated sportswear, enabling the creation of team uniforms, flag football gear, and branded apparel for clubs and fundraisers. The facility handles design, material selection, and construction using premium fabrics and techniques aimed at durability.

The company serves sports teams, brands, clubs, and fundraising organizations, providing customized uniforms and promotional wear. Flag football leagues are a noted segment, with dedicated uniform programs.

Apparel Forge differentiates itself by keeping all manufacturing steps under one roof in the United States, which it says ensures quality oversight and faster turnaround. The "Made in America" claim underscores its commitment to domestic production.

Apparel Manufacturing Co., Inc. has operated in Lilburn, Georgia, a suburb of Atlanta, since 1981. The family-owned business began as a two-person screen-print shop and has grown to a staff of fifty under the leadership of President and CEO Martin S. Tulis.

The company provides decorated apparel and promotional products from its in-house production facility. Core processes include screen printing, custom embroidery, and custom cut-and-sew, supplemented by a webstore fulfillment service for client orders. The facility handles both decoration of sourced blank goods and full custom sewing projects.

Apparel Manufacturing serves businesses and organizations across the United States and internationally, supplying branded merchandise for corporate identity programs, tradeshow giveaways, and employee uniform programs. Customers range from small companies to large enterprises seeking promotional items such as polo shirts, hoodies, caps, and technology accessories.

The company emphasizes a “no is not an option” service philosophy, positioning itself as a one-stop shop that combines production and logistics under one roof. Its longevity and family ownership are cited as foundations for consistent quality and responsiveness.

name: Applied Molding Technologies, LLC
old_description: Founded in 2006, Applied Molding Technologies delivers thermoplastic injection and thermoset compression, transfer and injection molding from Frederic, Wisconsin, serving customers globally, with new tooling built domestically and off-shore.
about:
Applied Molding Technologies, LLC was founded in 2006 in Frederic, Wisconsin. The company operates as a custom molder with no proprietary product lines, serving customers globally from its single facility.

The shop provides thermoplastic injection molding on all-electric presses ranging from 55 to 850 tons of clamp force, and thermoset compression, transfer, and injection molding on presses from 150 to 300 tons. It also offers value-added mechanical assembly including heat-staking, ultrasonic inserts, sub-assemblies, kitting, and ship-direct packaging. Production runs 24/7/365 on a four-shift rotation designed to minimize start-up and shut-down scrap. Tooling is sourced both domestically and off-shore, with in-house maintenance and repair.

Applied Molding serves a global customer base with varying technical, regulatory, and commercial requirements. Its thermoset capabilities target electrical and dielectric components as well as large or thick-section parts, while its thermoplastic work spans commodity and engineering-grade resins. The company scales engineering, quality, and program-management support to each customer's needs.

The business was built on the premise that domestic manufacturing could compete through a fundamentally different operating model rather than low-wage competition. Its founders designed the company for efficiency, customization, and adaptability—retaining core capabilities in-house while partnering for ancillary functions, and continuously revisiting processes through structured improvement.

old_description: Applied Plastics has been providing quality machined and fabricated plastic parts since 1976. All of our products are proudly manufactured at our 30,000 sf facility located in Portland Oregon. From this location we serve customers throughout the United States, Canada, and beyond. Applied Plastics has enjoyed success over the years as a result of our dedication to the needs of our customers. We produce quality plastic products for a wide range of industries and market segments. Ranging from retail displays to industrial plastics to extruded UHMW board stock, Applied Plastics is committed to quality, integrity, and excellence in the industries we serve.
about:
Applied Plastics was founded in 1976 in Portland, Oregon, where it operates a 30,000-square-foot manufacturing facility. The company has remained at this location for nearly five decades, serving customers across the United States, Canada, and internationally.

The shop specializes in machining and fabricating plastic parts, offering services that include acrylic fabrication, laser cutting and engraving, and precision cutting of full sheets to size. It also extrudes its own UHMW board stock and reprocesses recycled UHMW into usable material. The facility handles sheets, rods, and tubes in a variety of plastics, though headcount and annual volume are not disclosed.

Applied Plastics serves a range of markets, producing components for retail displays, industrial plastic applications, and extruded UHMW board stock. Its customer base spans multiple sectors that require custom plastic parts, from point-of-purchase fixtures to industrial wear components.

The company emphasizes a personal service guarantee, with machinists and fabricators working directly with clients on material selection and design. It also highlights environmental practices, including a near zero-waste operation that recycles acrylic scrap, extrudes recycled UHMW, and uses evaporative cooling and motion-activated lighting to reduce energy consumption.

about:
Arcco Power Systems is based in Baton Rouge, Louisiana, where it operates as a generator sales, service, rental, and parts provider. The company focuses on diesel, natural gas, and bi-fuel generators ranging from 10 kW to 3.2 MW in both stationary and portable configurations.

Arcco maintains a 60-unit portable generator fleet for catastrophic failures and can access a large inventory of rental sets during natural disasters. Its technician staff is on call 24 hours a day, 365 days a year, providing fuel cleaning, emergency repair, and temporary replacement for all makes and models of generators. The company also supplies automatic transfer switches and switchgear.

The company serves data centers, healthcare facilities, wastewater treatment plants, telecommunications providers, residential customers, educational institutions, manufacturing plants, oil and gas operations, and entertainment venues. It works with contractors to deliver power, shelter, and food-service operations to victims and first responders during emergencies.

Arcco states that its vision is to be the customer’s most generator partner, emphasizing an innovation- and strategy-focused approach that it describes as "Best in Class."

old_description: CUSTOMIZATION: In addition to the standard products shown on this page, Aries specializes in custom design and production. Special materials, platings, sizes, and configurations can be furnished, depending on quantity. NOTE: Aries reserves the right to change product specifications without notice.
about:
Aries Electronics Inc. was founded in 1972 in Bristol, Pennsylvania. The company has operated from this location for over five decades as a manufacturer of electrical sockets and interconnect products.

The company produces a broad range of interconnect components, including production IC sockets, test and burn-in sockets, high-frequency RF sockets, Correct-A-Chip® adapters, PCB and IC adapters, cable assemblies, and oscillator sockets. Its capabilities encompass custom engineering services and molding engineered plastics to extremely tight tolerances for devices on pitches below 0.2 mm. The catalog comprises over 150 full-specification product data sheets, and all hardware is stainless steel while molded socket components use UL 94V-0 rated PEEK or Ultem.

Aries serves original equipment manufacturers and semiconductor companies worldwide, supplying components for integrated circuit devices and electronic applications across industries such as telecommunications, computing, aerospace, and medical electronics. Customers range from businesses requiring standard catalog parts to those needing custom-designed sockets and adapters for specialized packaging or testing requirements.

The business was built on its patented Correct-A-Chip® technology, which eliminates the need for new PCB layouts when substituting integrated circuits, and on a focus on custom design and production for non-standard materials, platings, sizes, and configurations. The company emphasizes quality and performance in its interconnect solutions.

about:
Arizona Cottons operates from Tucson, Arizona, where Reuben Rosas has led the company for approximately 15 years. Rosas entered the custom apparel industry in 2005, spending four and a half years in screen printing and embroidery in Phoenix before joining Arizona Cottons. The business is organized as Arizona Cottons LLC.

The shop provides screen printing (both manual and automatic), embroidery, direct-to-film (DTF) printing, contract printing for B2B partners, clothing brand consulting, and full fulfillment including packaging and shipping. Production scales from single-digit runs through orders exceeding 10,000 pieces, categorized as small (1–144), medium (145–500), and large (501–10,000+). Equipment includes automatic screen printing presses, advanced embroidery machines, and DTF transfer systems.

Customers span corporate branding, promotional products, personalized gifts, startup clothing lines, and local businesses. Named clients include Desert Swarm Bee Removal, Rancho Sahuarita, and numerous small-business and personal-order accounts. The company emphasizes that no order is too small or too large.

Arizona Cottons differentiates itself with fast turnaround—citing a three-day completion for a last-minute order—consulting expertise for new apparel brands, and an end-to-end fulfillment model that handles printing, packing, and shipping under one roof.
